result.content:
---
# ocp4-rehearsal-lab, production overlay

# Destroy workflow. allow_simultaneous lets AAP run every destroy at once, and
# no cap is set, so a bulk cleanup launches the whole batch together.
destroy_workflow:
  allow_simultaneous: true
  concurrency_limit: null

# Each destroy resolves three DNS names separately before deleting them, so one
# job costs three ListResourceRecordSets calls rather than one batched lookup.
destroy_dns_lookups:
  - api
  - api-int
  - "*.apps"

dns_hosted_zone: dynamic.example-workshops.io

answer:
Root cause: the bulk cleanup saturated an AWS account-wide rate limit. It is not an outage, and the etcd growth is a consequence rather than a cause.

8 destroy jobs for `ocp4-rehearsal-lab` failed on controller `east`, all started within 21 seconds of each other and all failing on the same task, `host-ocp4-assisted-destroy : DNS entry`, with `(Throttling) ... ListResourceRecordSets ... Rate exceeded`. The account limit on that call is 5 requests per second.

The configuration is what turns a cleanup into a burst. `agd-v2/ocp4-rehearsal-lab/prod.yaml` sets `allow_simultaneous: true` with `concurrency_limit: null`, so AAP launches the whole batch together. And each destroy resolves three DNS names separately -- `api`, `api-int` and `*.apps` -- so one job costs three ListResourceRecordSets calls rather than one batched lookup. Eight jobs would not breach five per second; eight jobs each making three calls in the same instant does.

Route53 was responding normally. An isolated probe against the same hosted zone in the same window returned 3543 records in 412ms, so a regional outage is ruled out -- throttling and unavailability are different failures and this one is throttling.

The AnarchyRun build-up is downstream. etcd is at 4.77 GB of its 6 GB quota with 1184 failed or cancelled runs retained, because the cleanup policy removes successful runs only. Those objects accumulated because the runs failed, so it is a symptom of this incident rather than its cause -- it will stop growing once the destroys succeed, though the retained objects still need clearing.

Fix: cap concurrency on the destroy workflow, and batch the three DNS lookups into one call.
